title: Grade 4 French — Mon, May 25
description: Verbes en -ER — Day 1 of 5: What is a verb? The -ER pattern
subject: french

questions.question: What is a verb?
options: An action or state word (to run, to be, to eat)
questions.explanation: A verb describes an action (courir = to run) or a state (être = to be). Every French sentence has a verb.

questions.question: French verbs in the infinitive (dictionary form) end in:
questions.explanation: French infinitives end in -ER (parler), -IR (finir), or -RE (vendre). Most French verbs are -ER verbs.

questions.question: Which is an -ER verb?
questions.explanation: Parler (to speak) ends in -ER. Finir is -IR, Vendre is -RE, Avoir (to have) is irregular.

questions.question: To conjugate an -ER verb, you first:
options: Add endings to the infinitive directly
Remove the -ER to find the STEM, then add endings
questions.explanation: PARLER → remove -ER → STEM = PARL. Then add the endings: -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent.

questions.question: What is the stem of the verb JOUER (to play)?
questions.explanation: JOUER → remove -ER → stem = JOU. Endings are added to JOU: je joue, tu joues...

questions.question: The -ER endings are: je ___, tu ___, il ___, nous ___, vous ___, ils ___
questions.explanation: ER verb endings: je=-e, tu=-es, il/elle=-e, nous=-ons, vous=-ez, ils/elles=-ent. Learn these by heart!

questions.question: PARLER conjugated for 'je' (I speak)?
questions.explanation: Stem = PARL + -e (je ending) = je parle. (The 'e' is silent in pronunciation.)

questions.question: PARLER conjugated for 'tu' (you speak)?
questions.explanation: Stem PARL + -es (tu ending) = tu parles. (The 's' is silent in pronunciation.)

questions.question: PARLER conjugated for 'nous' (we speak)?
questions.explanation: Stem PARL + -ons (nous ending) = nous parlons. The -ons ending is unique and very regular.

questions.question: PARLER conjugated for 'ils' (they speak)?
questions.explanation: Stem PARL + -ent (ils/elles ending) = ils parlent. The -ent is SILENT in French!

questions.question: Full conjugation of PARLER — which is correct?
options: je parle / tu parles / il parle / nous parlons / vous parlez / ils parlent
je parles / tu parle / il parles / nous parlez / vous parlons / ils parlent
je parle / tu parle / il parle / nous parle / vous parle / ils parle
je parlent / tu parlons / il parlez / nous parles / vous parle / ils parle
questions.explanation: je parle, tu parles, il/elle parle, nous parlons, vous parlez, ils/elles parlent. This pattern applies to ALL regular -ER verbs.

questions.question: Translate: 'She speaks French.'
questions.explanation: Elle (she) → -e ending → elle parle. 'Elle parle français.'

questions.question: Translate: 'You (formal, vous) speak slowly.'
questions.explanation: Vous → -ez ending → vous parlez. 'Vous parlez lentement.' Vous is used for formal 'you' or plural 'you'.

questions.question: Why is the -ER verb pattern important to learn?
options: Over 90% of French verbs follow this pattern — learning it unlocks most French verbs
It is the same as English
questions.explanation: 90%+ of French verbs are -ER verbs. Once you learn the pattern (PARL+endings), you can conjugate thousands of verbs!

questions.question: MANGER (to eat) → je mange or je manges?
questions.explanation: MANGER → stem MANG + -e (je ending) = je mange. Same pattern as parler: je + stem + e.
